title: Coaction subspaces, highest lines and canonical contragredients
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be an affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Write $C=F[G]=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ with its canonical coordinate Hopf algebra, as in [def-sfb-coordinate-hopf-algebra]. Pullback along an affine group-scheme morphism $i:H\to G$ is the actual ring map $i^*:F[G]\to F[H]$ on global sections, which preserves the $F$-scalars because $i$ is over $F$. Tensor products and the coassociativity and counit predicates have the meanings in [def-sfb-hopf-action-module-data]. For an $F$-vector space $V$ and a rational coaction $c:V\to V\otimes_F C$, call an $F$-linear subspace $N$ stable if $c(N)$ lies in the image of $N\otimes_F C\to V\otimes_F C$. Call $c$ simple if $V\ne0$ and every stable subspace is $0$ or $V$. For an affine subgroup $i:H\to G$, define $V^H$ as the equalizer of $(1\otimes i^*)c$ and $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. For an affine torus $T$ and a character $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga], its character function is $\chi^*(t)\in F[T]$, with $t$ the Laurent coordinate. For inclusions $i_T:T\to G$, $i_U:U\to G$, say that $c$ has highest weight $\chi$ relative to $(T,U)$ if $\dim_F V^U=1$ and $(1\otimes i_T^*)c(v)=v\otimes\chi^*(t)$ for every $v\in V^U$. For finite-dimensional $V$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], set $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_F(V,F)$. A linear map $d:V^\vee\to V^\vee\otimes_F C$ is the canonical contragredient coaction if, for all $\ell\in V^\vee$ and $v\in V$, its contraction at $v$ equals $S$ applied to the contraction of $c(v)$ with $\ell$. Equivalently, after every scalar extension $(g\ell)(v)=\ell(g^{-1}v)$. All contractions determine $d$ uniquely; this predicate is not a choice of a dual action.
